subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing & SLOs — follow-up
messages:
From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@alphatech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing & SLOs

Marissa —

Thanks again for the call earlier. To help us move the Dedicated capacity evaluation forward, here are the items we discussed and a couple of clarifying questions:

- Business SLOs: we’re aiming for low-latency responses for our product search assistant. Wanted to confirm the target tiers: p50 ~80-120ms, p95 up to ~300ms (these are what we think is acceptable today).
- Expected workload: average 15 req/s with occasional peaks to ~50 concurrent users (roughly 50 concurrent streams). Attached is a one-day traffic sample (timestamped requests + prompt lengths) for engineering to use.
- Streaming: streaming responses are important for our UX (token-by-token). Is streaming supported on Dedicated with reserved throughput?
- GPU question: our infra lead asked if you’re recommending A100 or H100 for best latency at our scale and what reserved throughput guarantees look like.

Could you confirm the next steps and what you need from us to get a benchmark run scheduled?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Lee | CTO, Alphatech
Tom.lee@alphatech.com
Attachments: alphatech_traffic_sample.csv (CSV, ~2.5MB)

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing & SLOs

Tom —

Great to connect — appreciate the traffic sample. Below is a short post-call recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Recap (from our end):
- SLO targets: p50 target ~80ms, p95 target ~300ms (we noted your acceptable bands).
- Workload: baseline ~15 req/s, peaks ~50 concurrent streams; token lengths in sample average ~120 tokens with some longer docs.
- Streaming: supported — Dedicated does support streaming; we’re validating tail latency impact under streaming workloads as part of the perf run.
- GPU considerations: short answer: H100 generally gives better raw throughput/latency for large-context and high-concurrency workloads, but A100 is often more cost-efficient and performs well for many generator sizes. We should validate both with your real traffic.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood runs a dedicated capacity performance validation using your traffic sample across 2 GPU configs: A100 (40GB) and H100 (80GB) with our typical model variants.
2) We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, concurrency scaling, and streaming tail impact (KV cache warm vs cold).
3) We'll produce a sizing recommendation (reserved throughput options) and cost delta for each config plus suggested canary rollout steps.
4) Target to share initial benchmark results within 48-72 business hours after we have the test window confirmed.

What we need from you to start:
- Confirm the preferred test window (we prefer a 2-hour off-peak window to replay traffic; propose Tue 24 Mar 09:00-11:00 PT).
- Confirm model size / family you’re planning to run (or if you want us to test a couple of variants).
- Confirm streaming behavior (true streaming token-by-token vs chunked) and whether time-to-first-token or end-to-end is your primary metric.

I’ve attached a short benchmark plan and the workbook we use to capture results. Rafael and Aditya are looped for the engineering run. Rafael — can you pick a slot and confirm capacity to run both A100 and H100 profiles? Aditya/Neha — please note streaming test hooks and KV cache warm/cold toggles.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 15m if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0143
Attachments: dedicated_capacity_benchmark_plan.xlsx (Excel, ~120KB)

Team —

Forwarding Alphatech notes and traffic sample. Quick engineering ask before we confirm the test slot:

- Run both A100 (40GB) and H100 (80GB) profiles with:
  * Model variants: rlhf-13B and rlhf-70B (or closest open equivalent).
  * Measures: p50/p95/p99 latency (TTFT and end-to-end), tokens/sec, max sustainable concurrency, memory/KV cache behavior.
  * Streaming: replicate true token-by-token streaming and measure TTF-first-token vs tail latency under 50 concurrent streams.
  * Warm vs cold cache: do both (20 warm queries then cold).

Notes / engineering context: from prior runs we’re observing that H100 reduces p95 by roughly 20-35% at high concurrency for 70B-class models, but A100 is still cost-efficient and sometimes yields similar p50. We should validate network stack and batching config (continuous batching may increase p95 under streaming, so toggle batching sizes).

Attachments: rdw_benchmarks_gpus.pdf (report with baseline numbers). Rafael — can you provision the test cluster and confirm whether we need a reserved throughput ticket opened with infra? Also capture any model-variant fallback behavior if capacity constrained.

Thanks — will sync back to Alphatech after the run.

- Marissa

Thanks for the plan and for looping the eng team. We can confirm the Tue 24 Mar 09:00-11:00 PT window (apologies for the quick turnaround) — please proceed with the replay using the attached traffic sample. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- SLOs: final desired targets are p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 250-300ms. If those are achievable on H100 with the model we’re using, we’ll prioritize H100 for the initial Dedicated pool; but we’re open to A100 if the cost delta is significant and latency remains within target.
- Concurrency/throughput: design target is 50 concurrent streams sustained for 10-15 minute bursts; baseline sustained throughput ~15 req/s.
- Streaming: true token-by-token streaming is required; time-to-first-token is our most important UX metric, but tail latency matters too.

We’re available for a 30m sync Thu 26 Mar if you want to review preliminary numbers live. Rafael — let us know if you need additional traffic slices or model parameters.
